summary: Establish/advance use the owning adapter's nested savepoint, exact int64 strings and atomic bounded database increments; focused four SQLite groups and private SQLite/PostgreSQL compatibility/atomicity probes pass. A new read-helper gap independently reproduces: caught PostgreSQL server errors leave the outer transaction aborted yet it reports successful callback completion and rolls back preceding source work. Narrow storage approval requires read recovery or explicit transaction poison. No generated hooks/selection/worker or whole binding/Goal approval.

generated_output_probe_seam.meaning: Control seam is test-owned only. Original NUL repro used unmodified actual generated runtime. Valid-identity probe leaves generated transaction/helper code intact, substitutes SELECT 1 / 0 only for schedule read at the transaction driver boundary, and restores driver.begin.

findings.title: Recover or poison the source transaction when a schedule read fails
findings.cause: Unlike establish/advance, read_delivery_schedule_revision runs schema/read queries directly without nested client.transaction. Catching a PostgreSQL statement error leaves its server transaction aborted. The existing outer SQL.begin callback can then return normally and COMMIT completes as a rollback without the generated state being poisoned.
findings.observed: Actual generated persistence inserts Entry, caller catches delivery.schedule.read ERR_POSTGRES_SERVER_ERROR, outer transaction resolves 'callback_returned', and a separate connection finds no inserted row. The required no-false-ack assertion fails.
controls: Unmodified output plus accepted nonempty host identity '\u0000' triggers real server read failure; no driver mock.
Valid UUID identity plus private driver-level SELECT 1 / 0 injection reproduces the same result. Not dependent on malformed authored identity or simulated successful commit.
findings.concrete_required_change: Put ensureScheduleRevisions, SELECT and scheduleRevision validation inside client.transaction(async () => ...) for read as for the two writers, or mark the owning transaction poisoned on any unproved read/schema failure so outer completion cannot acknowledge success. Recoverable savepoint rollback may preserve prior source work; failed cleanup must keep the existing poison path. NUL validation alone does not fix valid-input server failures.
findings.regression: In a real disposable PG source transaction write a row, induce a schedule read server error, catch it, return. Require either recovered success with source row retained, or rejected/poisoned outer transaction with rollback. Never resolved success with absent source row. Retain SQLite, valid/missing reads, expired client and driver failure controls.

nonblocking_observations.result: Private SQLite Promise.allSettled of two nested advances triggers overlapping savepoint cleanup poison; outer transaction rejects and revision remains 1. This is fail-closed, not proof that such calls serialize successfully.
nonblocking_observations.constraint: Generated callers must await source helper operations sequentially. Concurrent separate source transactions are supported by the tested database/adapter path; no new owner gate.

nonblocking_observations.result: Helpers accept nonempty parameterized entity/id strings, not an authored capability. Cross-entity keys with identical identity strings stay isolated. They do not prove the entity exists or a due field was supplied.
nonblocking_observations.constraint: Future checked generator must bind exact entity/id and call only after successful relevant mutation in the same transaction. Host sequence A,A,B,A is storage counter evidence, not implemented due-hook/ABA receipt behavior.
